# GitHub Actions step parallelism rollout

Reviewed on 2026-10-07 against the [GitHub announcement](https://github.blog/changelog/2026-06-25-actions-steps-can-now-be-run-in-parallel/) and the [current workflow syntax](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/workflow-syntax).

The `parallel` step group runs its members concurrently in one job and waits for all of them before continuing. This rollout applies it to independent work that shares a runner and has no shared file or output dependency. The likely savings vary: environment-state reads avoid serial network waits, while QA and cache steps may contend for runner CPU or disk. Compare hosted run durations before drawing conclusions.

Both start after credentials are configured and write separate files under `$RUNNER_TEMP`. Preview history processing and all plan steps remain after the join. Both Preview reads retain their `synchronize` conditions. |

They use separate temporary fixtures or read repository files. All three remain required members of the same job.                                                                          |
| Unit-test job in [`quality-assurance.yml`](../workflows/quality-assurance.yml)                                                                                                                 | After dependency setup, run `Build packages` beside `Restore cache`. They write workspace outputs and `~/.cache/ms-playwright`. Browser installation and the existing unit-test command follow the group.                                                                                                    |
| Preview `accounts-client` job in [`deploy-to-environment.yml`](templates/deploy-to-environment.yml)                                                                                            | Start Playwright cache restore in the background after checkout, then run the existing dependency fragment, including package builds. Wait for the cache before browser installation, client build, and smoke tests.                                                                                         |
| Scheduled production tests in [`production-scheduled-tests.yml`](../workflows/production-scheduled-tests.yml)                                                                                  | In both `setup` and `accounts-tests`, group the caller's `Setup dependencies` action with Playwright `Restore cache`. The composite action itself remains unchanged. Browser installation and smoke tests remain after the join in `accounts-tests`.                                                         |

## Hosted validation

On the next CI runs, inspect the delivery-catalog and unit-test jobs in Quality Assurance, plus a Preview pull request run. Confirm the Preview state reads skip on the initial `opened` event and both run on `synchronize`, with history processing and planning after the group. Compare native step and job timestamps with comparable earlier runs, and record browser-cache hit or miss for QA, Preview, and both scheduled jobs. Confirm the same two Playwright shards pass. Check Develop and Production on the next normal Release delivery and the scheduled workflow on its next occurrence. Do not add temporary timing steps or claim a speed improvement until hosted measurements support it.

## Deferred candidate

Accounts storage teardown in [`teardown-environment.yml`](templates/teardown-environment.yml) could remove its Download and Upload buckets concurrently before stack teardown. The current shell stops at the first failed removal; a parallel group would let the other removal continue and report failure only at the join. Keep this deferred because it changes partial-cleanup behavior.

## Keep existing boundaries

- The top-level QA gates already run as independent jobs under [ADR 0010](../docs/adr/0010-run-qa-quality-gates-in-parallel.md). Keep their required-check boundaries. Keep workspace test concurrency bounded by [ADR 0009](../docs/adr/0009-bound-qa-workspace-test-concurrency.md), and leave Playwright commands, configuration, and shards unchanged.
- Deployment Unit jobs already follow the generated `needs` graph. Do not parallelize dependent deployments inside a job; Core communications, for example, imports the `HostedZoneId` export from Core infrastructure.
- Keep the dependency-cache chain in order: restore exact installed dependencies, restore Yarn archives on a miss, install immutably, then build required workspace packages. The separate Playwright browser cache can overlap independent work and must join before browser installation or tests.
- Keep CodeQL initialization before build and analysis, Release publication before Release Plan construction, Renovate cache preparation before Renovate, and Playwright browser preparation before tests.
- Do not add `parallel` or `background` inside the local composite [`setup-dependencies` action](../actions/setup-dependencies/action.yml). GitHub does not allow those keywords inside a composite action; apply parallel grouping at the workflow level.
- Preserve production Storybook baseline reporting after the successful GitHub Pages deployment record. Running it beside Pages publication would change the documented behavior.

## Syntax and failure behavior

Use `parallel` for a self-contained group that should finish before the next step. GitHub defines it as background steps plus an implicit wait. A failed member fails the group unless that step has `continue-on-error: true`; all members are allowed to finish before the group reports failure. Background-step outputs and environment changes become available only after the applicable wait. At most ten background steps may run concurrently in one job. A `wait` step always runs and does not support `if`, so conditions belong on the background step itself.

The implemented workflows use `parallel` for environment reads, catalog checks, the QA package/cache pair, and scheduled setup/cache pairs. Preview Accounts client uses `background` plus `wait` to overlap browser-cache restore with dependency setup. No workflow uses `wait-all` or `cancel`.
